description: ETHEL is a solo engineering project designing a closed-loop life support system for Mars. It integrates a 3-phase dynamic atmospheric recycling reactor, Sabatier-biocatalytic CO2 conversion, and ISRU architecture with mathematical models, C++ logic, and habitat docs.
summary: Aethel is a closed-loop bio-regenerative and In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) habitat architecture for Mars that bridges human psychology with planetary engineering. By integrating biophilic crop cultivation (Lens culinaris, microgreens) with the advanced Aethel Oxygen Engine (cyclonic Sabatier reduction, water electrolysis, and 3-phase thermal stabilization), the system simultaneously sustains life support, water recycling, and crew psychological resilience. Furthermore, Aethel v2 leverages surplus gases to power fuel cells and a roof-mounted Deep Space Optical Communication (DSOC) laser array, establishing an uninterrupted interplanetary data and energy grid.
details:
Aethel is an advanced, closed-loop In-Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) and bio-regenerative habitat architecture designed for long-duration Martian missions. Moving beyond traditional metallic shelters, Aethel integrates biological life support with engineering systems to optimize crew health, resource recycling, and interplanetary communication.

Key Innovations:

* Bio-Regenerative Life Support (CELSS): Cultivates high-yield crops (Lens culinaris, Coriandrum sativum, Lactuca sativa, Spinacia oleracea, Brassica juncea) to meet metabolic needs, reduce water consumption through transpiration, and provide psychological sanctuary.

* Aethel Oxygen Engine: A cyclonic ISRU core combining Sabatier reduction with catalytic water electrolysis for continuous oxygen generation and methane production for Mars Ascent Vehicle (MAV) propellant.

* 3-Phase Thermal Stabilization (MCHEX): Implements a deterministic 30-second thermal flush cycle to suppress thermodynamic overshoot and protect the catalytic matrix during peak loads.

* Energy-to-Data Synthesis Grid (DSOC): Routes surplus oxygen and hydrogen through a High-Efficiency Fuel Cell unit to generate continuous electrical power and drive a roof-mounted Deep Space Optical Communication (DSOC) laser array for high-bandwidth interplanetary internet links.
